research_rationale:
EO 13109 (signed 1998-12-17; 63 FR 70631, Federal Register of 1998-12-22, FR Doc. 98-34034) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13109.txt. It closes executive departments and agencies and excuses employees from duty on one named day (Christmas Eve, December 24, 1998), lets agency heads keep offices open for stated reasons, and treats that day as within the scope of EO 11582 and 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) for pay and leave. Every command is tied to that single day, so each clause ends by its own terms on 1998-12-24 (inclusive reading; the exclusive reading would end the commands when that day began). A by-number search of the held order texts finds no later order citing this order, and the three machine searches record no later amendment, revocation or supersession. The held text is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF; the PDF page images are not held, so identity (printed number, title, signing date and FR Doc. number) was checked on the text layer against the census register row.

savings.reason: Employees excused from duty on the named day were excused under the order, and pay and leave for that day are governed by EO 11582 and the cited statutes, which the order only applied to the day; those accrued pay and leave effects rest on the cited authorities and do not keep the order operative after 1998-12-24. No held source shows any pending matter, exception or savings clause in the order.
